variables.claim_asserts: Across plants and animals, few germ nuclei have haploid chromosome number n below 6 and fewer still have n above 16.
variables.test_measures: Fractions of CCDB plant and ACC animal taxa with parsed haploid n below 6, from 6 through 16, and above 16, at species and genus resolutions.

modality.note: Curated chromosome-count databases directly measure gametic n in plants and animals; using N where available and 2N/2 otherwise matches the claim's germ-nucleus variable.

assumptions.note: The 10% support and 25% refutation thresholds quantify vague words, but observed upper-tail fractions of 34.4% for plant species and 38.9% for animal species are plainly incompatible with 'fewer still' and exceed the lower tails in both kingdoms.

scope.claim_scope: Haploid chromosome numbers in germ nuclei across plants and animals.
scope.test_scope: Species represented in all four CCDB plant major groups and the ACC animal database, summarized once per species and once per genus.

reasons: The test bins the claim's exact variable, haploid n, at the claim's exact boundaries n < 6 and n > 16.
Species-level upper tails are 0.344 for plants and 0.389 for animals, versus lower tails of 0.016 and 0.086; the same inversion appears at genus level.
Although the verdict rule uses genus medians to damp sampling bias, the reported species-level figures independently meet the refutation criterion and preserve organisms as the unit.
CCDB and ACC sampling biases limit population prevalence estimates but do not replace chromosome number with a proxy or change the plant-and-animal modality.
what_would_change_it: Use a phylogenetically stratified, species-level census or probability sample of plant and animal haploid chromosome numbers; a faithful result would change only if its estimated n > 16 fractions became genuinely small and below the n < 6 fractions.
